govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAMarchettiVic:
Victor Marchetti had been a high-ranking CIA officer, a special assistant near the top of the agency, before he became its most troublesome defector in print. Penthouse magazine framed its interview with him as an open letter to the CIA.

Marchetti talks about covert operations, including the destabilization of Chile, from inside knowledge of the building he had served. His book The CIA and the Cult of Intelligence had already made legal history through the government's effort to censor it before publication. The interview is preserved as part of the seventies exposure wave, when former officers became the agency's loudest critics.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MertzMichaelVic:
An unnamed writer addressed this letter to 'Bud' on April 15, 1980. Its subject is what the writer calls the heroin angle. The letter discusses reporter Les Payne and 'The Heroin Trail,' a newspaper investigation of the drug trade. It also mentions the French SDECE, that country's foreign intelligence service. The author's name cannot be recovered from the garbled scan.

Heroin trafficking threads run through assassination research of the period, linking Marseille, intelligence services, and exile politics in researchers' theories. This letter shows one reader working those connections in private correspondence. It names its sources and its suspicions, even if the file cannot name the man who wrote it down.
